newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds eked out small gains despite declines in German Bund futures, which were pressured by latest uncertainty about Europe's planned single currency.

One Swiss bond trader termed comments Thursday by newly-elected French prime minister Lionel Jospin as "horrible for financial markets." Jospin, speaking in a keynote address to French parliament, outlined plans to create jobs. His emphasis on jobs rather than budget tightening raised questions about France's committment to meeting strict budget criteria for membership in the new Europepan currency, the euro.
Traders said Bund weakness could spill over into Swiss franc bonds if it continues.

Longer maturities were supported by strength in the short end of the market. One trader said the Swiss franc's rise was helpful, given expectations the Swiss National Bank (SNB) will stay generous to counter any significant Swiss franc gains. SNB officials speaking at an annual summer briefing for journalists said it was still too early in the recovery cycle for the SNB to tighten. The SNB also reconfirmed its committment to combatting currency "distortions" -- such as a strong franc -- which could hurt an export-led recovery.

SNB board member Bruno Gehrig said that the SNB has, in the past year, focused more on the rates set on its short-term money market operations as opposed to money aggregates to steer its day-to-day policy. But he said money aggegates remained important for setting long-term policy.
Conf futures CONFc1 up two at 120.33.
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 up eight at 98.54.
